title: Playbook: Graceful shutdown of legacy header-versioned transport and compatibility adapter
creator: Liam O'Connor
description: This PRD describes the phased retirement of the legacy header-versioned transport (X-Transport-Version: v0) and the accompanying compatibility adapter (compat-proxy) that has been used by older SDKs and internal customers. The goal is to remove the legacy transport surface while providing a robust safety net for customers still on older clients: a time-bound compat-adapter, a concierge migration offering for enterprise accounts, telemetry gates to guard quality regressions, and documentation + SDK patches to accelerate migration.
background: The header-versioned transport was introduced early in the product lifecycle to support incremental protocol changes. Over time this created branching client codepaths and server-maintenance overhead. Recent runtime optimizations and unified-inference features require a single canonical transport. Several high-usage clients (internal and 3rd-party enterprise) still depend on X-Transport-Version: v0 and the compat-proxy. Multiple incidents in Q4 2024 tied to patch drift on the compat-proxy increased maintenance cost and limited new runtime kernel rollout velocity.
scope_inbound: 1) Provide a 12-week staged deprecation timeline and customer migration playbook. 2) Build an opt-in 'compatibility concierge' program for top 25 enterprise customers to assist migration. 3) Implement server-side telemetry and signal gates to detect regressions when compat-proxy is removed. 4) Ship SDK client patches and a node/python adapter that rewrites legacy headers to the unified transport. 5) Create public docs, migration checklist, and CLI migration helper.
scope_outbound: We are not refactoring the underlying model routing or authentication model as part of this work. The legacy transport removal will not change response formats; any structured-output work is out of scope. We will not auto-migrate customer server components or modify customer data stores.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Compat-proxy can be put behind a feature flag and fully disabled in staging without >0.5% error-rate increase on canary clients.
A2: SDKs (node/python/go) have published patched releases with clear migration guides and automated header rewrite adapter with <5ms p50 latency overhead in integration test harness.
A3: Top 25 enterprise customers identified and onboarded into 'compatibility concierge' within first 4 weeks of announcement.
A4: Telemetry gates (latency, 5xx, hallucination surrogate) defined and wired into rollout pipeline; rollbacks automatically triggered when thresholds exceeded.
A5: Public docs and migration CLI are published and linked from dashboard notices; at least 75% of active legacy clients have upgraded or scheduled migration within 8 weeks of announcement.
A6: Migration runbook and rollback checklist reviewed and approved by Support, Security, and Reliability teams.
A7: Final shutdown date communicated with 30 days notice to remaining customers and tickets closed for compat-proxy removal.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Week -2..0): Finalize docs, SDK patches, and define telemetry gates. Phase 1 (Week 0): Announce deprecation to all customers and create console banners and email lanes. Phase 2 (Week 1..4): Offer concierge signups to enterprise customers; run in-place compatibility tests and assist with SDK upgrades. Phase 3 (Week 5..8): Begin throttling compat-proxy on non-concierge customers and enable aggressive telemetry monitoring. Phase 4 (Week 9..10): Disable compat-proxy in staging and selected regions; hold for 2 weeks. Phase 5 (Week 11..12): Final disable globally and remove server-side support. Allow rolling rollback windows if telemetry gates breach. Postmortem and customer completion report due 2 weeks after final disable.
telemetry_gates: Latency: p95 increase >10% over baseline across canary clients triggers rollback
Error rate: 5xx or disconnect rate >0.2% absolute increase triggers immediate pause
Quality surrogate: increase in rerank/regression alerts on a curated prompt set >1.5x baseline triggers investigation
Adoption signals: >=75% of active legacy client footprint upgraded or scheduled by week 8 required to proceed to final disable
customer_communication: Initial announcement email + console banner (Week 0), followed by weekly migration digest for signups. Dedicated account outreach for enterprise concierge with a migration SLA. 30-day final-notice email before shutoff. Public FAQ and migration guide with code samples (node/python/go) and CLI helper. Support playbook for CS and SE with escalation paths and rollback instrument commands.
migration_tools: 1) header-rewrite adapter npm/pypi package (lightweight middleware that rewrites X-Transport-Version to unified transport header). 2) CLI migration helper that scans logs to identify legacy header traffic and suggests migration batch sizes. 3) Sandbox test harness to exercise patched SDKs against a canary environment with telemetry reports.
docs_and_sdk_tasks: Release node SDK v5.3.0 with opt-in header-rewrite adapter
Release python SDK v3.8.0 with automated deprecation logs and adapter
Create quickstart: migration-playbook.md with sample curl, node, python flows
engineering_notes: ENG leads to implement toggleable compat-proxy flag, a canary region, and automatic rollback hooks in the deployment pipeline. Ensure feature flag exposes metrics for per-customer traffic shard. Backend implementers must instrument the legacy header parsing path to emit migration_id and client_sdk_version. Coordinate with infra to reserve a maintenance window for final removal and to validate kernel compatibility after removal.
milestones: M3: Concierge onboarding complete for top customers (2025-04-07)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Large customers with custom proxies won't upgrade in time — Mitigation: Offer concierge migration and temporary tenancy for extended support under exception contract
Risk: Unexpected latency regressions when compat-proxy removed — Mitigation: Multi-stage canary with automated rollback and stress tests in staging
Risk: Telemetry blindspots for third-party SDKs — Mitigation: Expand logging surface to include SDK version and provide a lightweight opt-in telemetry agent for customers
